rationales.data-access.missing-org-filter: Spec 62 Amendment A1: the rule is declared-or-discovered, never the deleted English fallback (commit f6493af / Spec 44). Tenancy here is DECLARED via `schemas` (Tier 2 — a table carrying an org_id column), for both the Japanese tables (注文/商品) and the English-named tables (orders/users/products). Declaring the English names in this fixture's config is the honest replacement for the fallback: the fixture now states its tenant set explicitly instead of relying on `requiresOrgFilter` hardcoding a word list. Proof the fallback is gone: `requiresOrgFilter` (UniversalDataAccessAnalyzer.ts:1743) consults only `orgFilterTables` (Tier 1) and `schemas` (Tier 2); an English table name with no declaration fires nothing.

description: Non-English identifiers — mixed Portuguese, German, Japanese, French. DB access via drizzle-orm provenance only (no mock db). All six tables (注文/商品 + orders/users/products) are DECLARED tenant via the schemas config, each carrying an org_id column. 12 ground-truth violations: 9 missing-org-filter (every tenant-table query filters on something other than org_id, or not at all), 2 unfiltered-query (the two genuinely filterless reads — `SELECT * FROM users` in abfragen.ts and `SELECT * FROM 商品` in kuesutori.ts), 1 loop-query (abfragen.ts N+1). The WHERE-clause queries (user_id/status/type/role/category) are correctly NOT unfiltered-query — they have a filter, just not an org filter. 3 known-misses: missing-auth (French autoriser), missing-sanitization (French nettoyer), open-closed (German verarbeiten) — cross-analyzer gaps deferred to Spec 15 neighborhood.
